subject: Feasibility: HIPAA + FERPA addenda for HS Clinic pilot
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@hsclinic.org>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procure@hsclinic.org, alan.rivera@hsclinic.org
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0500
Subject: Inquiry: HIPAA/FERPA scope for pilot with Redwood

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at HS Clinic is excited about the pilot. Before we move to a technical kickoff our legal and compliance teams asked for clarification on a few items around regulated data:

- We expect the pilot to ingest student health records that may include immunization and visit notes tied to student IDs (FERPA + limited PHI). Can Redwood operate under a combined addendum (BAA + FERPA addendum) or do you treat these as separate agreements?
- Subprocessors: we need a current list and the ability to review any that will process PHI/education data.
- Data residency: pilot must keep data in US-only regions. Is that supported for hosted pilots, or would we need Dedicated/Private?
- Encryption and key management requirements: can you confirm support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for both at-rest and in-transit?

If you can provide a short feasibility note and attach your standard addendum we can route to our counsel. We aim to start ingest the week of 11/29.

Appreciate a quick read — attaching HS Clinic's baseline DPA redline for context (HSClinic_DPA_redline_20261111.pdf will follow).

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Director, Legal & Compliance
HS Clinic Network
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@hsclinic.org>, procure@hsclinic.org
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: HIPAA/FERPA scope for pilot with Redwood

Hi Samantha — thanks for outlining this. Short answer: we can support a combined DPA + BAA + FERPA addendum for the pilot, but there are tradeoffs depending on deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

Quick clarifying questions to help scope the feasibility note and timeline:
1) Will student identifiers be pseudonymized prior to sending, or do you need us to handle linking to the student ID?
2) Are any model outputs considered part of the student record (i.e., will you write generated content back to your system-of-record)?
3) Expected TPS/volume for the pilot and peak concurrency (this affects batching/latency and whether Dedicated is recommended).

Next steps from our side: Marissa will draft a short feasibility memo and attach our current DPA + subprocessor list. I’m also looping in Vivek for residency/ops constraints and Neha for contract redline coordination.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_draft_v2.pdf, subprocessors_20261110.csv

Can we schedule a 30-minute legal sync on Thu 11/12?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@hsclinic.org>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: alan.rivera@hsclinic.org, procure@hsclinic.org
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: HIPAA/FERPA scope for pilot with Redwood

Hi Olga — quick answers below. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

- Pseudonymization: for the pilot we can pseudonymize a subset but need Redwood to support later linking for the full integration; so we require that your platform can accept a reversible tokenization under strict KMS controls.
- Model outputs: initially outputs will not be written back to student records; we will evaluate after pilot.
- Volume: expected 1200 records/day, bursts up to 8 TPS.
- Residency: must be US-only for both storage and model execution.

We attached our redline (HSClinic_DPA_redline_20261111.pdf). For the legal sync please include someone from ops who can answer residency and subprocessor isolation questions.

Thanks,
Samantha

Subject: Re: Inquiry: HIPAA/FERPA scope for pilot with Redwood

Hi Samantha — looping in the technical/ops perspective and a short feasibility summary below.

Feasibility summary (pilot constraints & recommendations):
- Residency: Hosted (multi-tenant) can be configured to store and process data in a US-only region, but for full contractual residency guarantees and exclusive compute pools we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC) for the pilot. Dedicated gives predictable throughput (handles your 8 TPS bursts) and isolates KV caches/subprocessors.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists current subprocessors and processing roles. Any subprocessors that touch PHI or education data can be fenc ed via Dedicated and contractually limited. We support pre-notification + 14-day review for high-risk subprocessors.
- Keys: we support KMS integration for customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption; for model execution we can integrate with HSM-backed keys in Dedicated/Private.
- Agreements: we can produce a combined DPA + BAA + FERPA addendum. Our standard DPA covers data flows; the FERPA addendum will include the education-specific clauses you requested (access controls, record-keeping, and parental-consent language).

Requested next steps:
1) Legal review of our Redwood_DPA_draft_v2.pdf and your redline (you mentioned HSClinic_DPA_redline_20261111.pdf).
2) Ops call (30 min) — proposed Thu 11/12 10:00 AM ET — to confirm residency and subprocessor isolation.
3) Decision on deployment mode (Hosted with US-only controls vs Dedicated). If Dedicated, we’ll scope capacity and provide a cost estimate.

Attachments: subprocessors_20261110.csv, Redwood_DPA_draft_v2.pdf

Link: dataflow diagram and initial M.A.P. (mutual action plan) at https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleDataflowDiagram

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
